## Rule

Template-stamp (derived from examples 2026-07-11). Each 10×10 grid has ONE small colored
"template" block (cells that are non-0 AND non-5) plus several gray (color-5) placeholder
regions of identical dimensions. Output = copy the template's pattern into every 5-region
(preserving relative position within the block); the template itself and all background 0s
are unchanged. Placement is data-dependent (template position + region positions/count vary
per input) → a Conv/render floor (traps §132), NOT a free-output separable formulation.

## Algorithm sketch

Live graph `bianfu3` (19 nodes, opset 18, ~1558 real cost):
1. `Conv(input,[0..9], k[1,1], pads[0,0,-20,-20])` → F32 [1,1,10,10]: channel-index weighted
   sum decodes color AND the negative pad crops 30×30 canvas→10×10 in one free op (#35).
2. `Equal(==5)` → is-5 mask; `Clip(0,1)` → foreground mask; `Where(is5,0,fg)` → template-only mask.
3. `MaxPool(k[10,10])` argmax → flat index of template anchor; `Div/Mod 10` → (row,col).
4. `Slice(pad(colorgrid), starts=anchor+3, ends=anchor-12, step[-1,-1])` → reversed template kernel.
5. `QLinearConv(fg, fixed 2×2)` → region-anchor map; `QLinearConv(anchors, template-kernel)` → stamp.
6. Two `QLinearConv(1×1)` re-encode to 10-channel one-hot; final `pads[0,0,20,20]` restores 30×30.
